title: ADR-NN-<slug>.md (plan decision record) runtime body-structure contract
description: Hook-consumable runtime artifact for plan-tree Architecture Decision Records at <plan>/decisions/ADR-NN-<slug>.md. The k8s ValidatingAdmissionPolicy paramKind for the ADR record type. Decisions that would otherwise be buried in spec prose / context-packets / handoffs become short, immutable, individually-addressable, supersession-tracked records — the RFC→ADR best-practice borrow (Nygard ADR format). Matcher convention declared at governance/plans-rules.json :: decision_records; manifest pointer array at schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json :: decision_records[].

_design_notes.consumer: librarian plan-index (decision-record enumeration) + future R-27-adjacent advisory; manifest pointer round-trips via schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json :: decision_records[]
_design_notes.lockstep_pair: governance/plans-rules.json :: decision_records (convention) + schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json :: decision_records[] (manifest pointer shape)
_design_notes.evolution_protocol: R-37 atomic lockstep — this runtime artifact + plans-rules.json decision_records convention + plan-manifest-schema.json decision_records[] + governance/_index.json coupled_surfaces move in one commit

filename_rationale: ADR-NN-<slug>.md — NN is a monotonic two-digit (or wider) creation-order ordinal within the plan's decisions/ dir; slug is a short kebab-case decision name. Ordinal is immutable once published (like task IDs).
immutable_rationale: An accepted ADR is an immutable record of a decision made at a point in time. A decision change does NOT edit the original — it creates a NEW ADR that supersedes the prior one (the prior ADR's Status flips to `superseded-by-ADR-NN`; the new ADR references what it supersedes in Context). Mirrors the RFC→ADR supersession chain; distinct from the in-place amendment pattern used by spec.md.

h1.match_rule: must begin with the ADR ordinal — `# ADR-NN: <Title>`
h1.rationale: Heading carries the addressable ordinal; readers and the manifest pointer key on ADR-NN.

status_line.value_enum_note: Status enum reconciled to the MADR-canonical {proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated} + superseded-by-ADR-NN form, across the three coupled surfaces (this contract + governance/plans-rules.json :: decision_records.status_enum + schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json :: decision_records[].status) under R-37 documentary lockstep. MADR captures rejected options as first-class records.
status_line.rationale: A single status token (or the concrete supersession form). The supersession form embeds the superseding ADR ordinal so the chain is human-readable; the manifest pointer carries the bare token + a separate superseded_by field.

section_semantics.Context: The forces at play — the situation, constraints, and tensions that make a decision necessary. Factual and neutral; does not state the decision.
section_semantics.Decision: The decision made, stated in active voice ('We will …'). One decision per ADR.
section_semantics.Consequences: What becomes easier and what becomes harder as a result — including follow-on work, accepted trade-offs, and anything a superseding ADR would need to revisit.

considered_options.heading: Considered Options
considered_options.required_when: the Decision had real contested alternatives (a genuine fork with more than one viable path)
considered_options.placement: between Context and Decision (the alternatives the Decision chose among)
considered_options.rationale: MADR's load-bearing thesis is that capturing the REJECTED options + their trade-offs is what makes a record valuable later. Required only on contested decisions; preserves the size_limits.max_lines 120 cap (long rationale stays in context-packets/ or the spec).

supersession.mechanism: new ADR supersedes old; old ADR Status → `superseded-by-ADR-NN`; new ADR names the superseded ADR in its Context

size_limits.rationale: ADRs are short by design — one decision, the forces behind it, and its consequences. Long rationale belongs in context-packets/ or the spec; the ADR is the durable record, not the working material.
